title: Two Ledgers, Both Ways
summary: The two lists you liked now carry the section alone: the line on the left, the big statement and the red button are gone, so 'Built for' and 'Not for' are the headline, with the one sentence that explains them held beside them as you scroll.
story: Straight after 'It starts with the audit', this shows the audit is a gate that works both ways, with 'Someone will own it' open opposite 'Outsource-it-forever'; the next section answers with 'Sound like you?'.
motion: entrance (still beat, reveal only, about 2s): the label fades in, the lede rises 12px, then the link. 'Built for' rises out of its mask, its ink rule draws left to right, and its + and the 'We say yes when · 03' line fade in. Its three rows cascade in (80ms apart). 'Not for' and its rows follow the same way, 400ms behind.

the one moment: once the rows have landed, the two resting rows open in reading order. 'Someone will own it' opens at 1.3s and 'Outsource-it-forever' at 1.6s (360ms each): the answer drops into its place under the row title and the + turns to −. Those two rows keep their open height from the first frame, so nothing below them moves while it lands. There is no drawing, no packet and nothing loops.

interaction: each ledger opens in place, one row at a time; clicking the open row closes it. Hovering a row nudges its title 6px right; a Not-for title goes from muted to ink on hover or when open. Rows are real buttons with expanded/collapsed state for screen readers, closed answers can't be tabbed into, and the rows and the link both show a 1px focus outline. A click in one ledger stops only that ledger's timed reveal; clicking a row that is still waiting to open simply opens it.

on the live site: the reveal plays once when the section scrolls into view, with no pin, and the section's height never changes while it plays (so the CTA below never jumps). The left column (label, lede, link) is sticky, 128px from the top of the screen. It stays beside the ledgers while they scroll past, then leaves with the section. Under reduced motion the section renders its final state at once (the two rows open), with no entrance and no timers.
standalone mockup: the same reveal, resting by about 2s.
addressed: 'I don't understand the point of that animated line on the left… confusing': the line is gone, along with its gate, its callouts and its figure caption. The left side now holds one plain sentence: the audit is a gate, and it works in both directions.

'I really like the layout… the rest is pretty good': the two ledgers are unchanged in shape, with 'Built for' and 'Not for' at the same 42px, one row open in each and the muted Not-for list. A small + and – now sit beside the two headings so yes and no read at a glance.

The headings are the headline: the 88px statement is gone, and so are the red button and the 'Sound like you?' closing row. That line now opens the final section directly below, so the page asks once, not twice in a row.

Sharper rows: 'Someone will own it' (the yes) now rests open opposite 'Outsource-it-forever' (the no). Kelwin turns down the client who would make it a permanent vendor, which backs up the handover promise from the decline side.

Following your FAQ note, an open row shows its answer as plain text with no heading above it, so the row title stays the strongest line. 'Outsource-it-forever' no longer says 'dependency by design' twice: the short line beside the title carries that phrase, and the answer reads 'Nobody inside will own the system — declined.'
Nothing in this section is red except the small label square, which leaves the red for the final section.
notes: Layout at 1440: a sticky column in cols 1–4 (position: sticky, top 128px, not a pin) holds the label (an h2 with the kit's label style, since there is no statement), the 20px lede and the link 'Three situations, told from inside →' (/who-we-work-with). Cols 6–12 hold the two ledgers. The right column starts 36px down, so the lede's first line and 'Built for' share a baseline; measured in both skins. Each head sits on the ledger's own columns: the mono sign is in the index column, and the 42px heading starts on the row-title edge, so the row titles hang from it. 'Built for' sits on an ink rule, 'Not for' on a quieter one. Round 2's dashed rule was the fork's branch, and dashed now means 'drafted by Kelwin' in the handover. Row columns are index 72 · title 1.5fr · descriptor 1fr · toggle 20, so 'Real revenue, felt ceiling' stays on one line in both skins. Open answers are 17px ink, one sentence per line on desktop, and flow normally on phones. Every band and line height is a whole pixel, so the section is exactly 1050px tall with no hairline seam. Entrance: the two resting rows keep their open height throughout, and only their answers are held back and then revealed (opacity plus an 8px drop, 360ms). The earlier build collapsed them and re-expanded them, which pushed 'Not for' down by about 100px while it was still rising and changed the section's height by about 200px on the stitched page. Signs: the + / − mono marks are set in JetBrains Mono at 28px, unboxed, in --fg-3, so their centre sits on the heading's x-height. The minus is an en dash, because this mono build draws U+2212 like its hyphen (320 units wide against the plus's 470) and it read as stray punctuation. They are text glyphs, visibly heavier than the thin drawn row toggles at the right, so they read as yes/no signs, not buttons. Copy check: lede (★, verbatim from STORY §2) is assembled from QualifyFlow ('it works in both directions'), the /who-we-work-with lede ('the honest list of who we send away') and FitStrip ('before we say yes'). F-01 'Real revenue, felt ceiling' is FirmFit's ZONE_CRITERIA title, and 'The motion works.' is the first clause of its description. Its body is round-2 X's F-01 line ('Growth is real, just not predictable yet. There's a motion we can measure, then make repeatable.'), as STORY specifies, rather than FirmFit's own ('…growth has stopped compounding. That's an architecture problem.'). That line would add a third 'compound' (the page cap is two) and repeat the hero's thesis. F-02 'Someone will own it' and its body are FirmFit verbatim. Its descriptor 'An operator inside.' is STORY's trim of FirmFit's 'an internal operator', not a verbatim line; kept because it mirrors D-01's 'Nobody inside'. D-01 'Outsource-it-forever' is FirmFit's ANTIFIT probe, capitalised. Its descriptor 'Dependency by design.' and its body 'Nobody inside will own the system — declined.' split FirmFit's ANTIFIT line ('nobody inside will own the system — dependency by design, declined') between them, word for word, so the open row no longer repeats 'dependency by design'. STORY gives the full line as the body; this is a faithful trim (review fix). F-03, D-02 and D-03 are round-2 X verbatim, as are 'Built for', 'Not for', 'We say yes when', 'We decline when' and the 03 counts. No numbers, years, clients or results were added; there are no drawings, so there is no Specimen block. Live-page note: the column is truly sticky, which can't show in a static image. The review tool's full-page capture scrolls to the bottom first, so in home-*-full.png this column appears at the bottom of its travel, beside 'Not for'. Scrolled normally, it sits beside 'Built for' and follows the reader. Capturing after scrolling back to the top would show its true resting place. Phones (≤760px): not sticky, stacked, 16px gutters, descriptors under the titles, no horizontal scroll (checked at 390px).
